findings.title: Inverted condition for organization slug and requestedSlug
findings.body: The original code spread `slug` when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` and `requestedSlug` when billing was disabled. The rewrite `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` flips that logic, so with billing enabled the org gets a real slug immediately and with billing disabled it doesn't. This is an unrelated behavior change to organization creation that the PR description does not mention. Revert to the original semantics.

findings.title: Unguarded access to first destination calendar can throw
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` can yield `undefined` when the array is empty, but line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Any event with location Google Meet and no destination calendar (e.g. organizer has no destinationCalendar, or the array is `[]`) will throw a TypeError during create. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: updateEvent loses calendar id when no externalCalendarId is passed
findings.body: The fallback is now `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, this compares each destination's externalId against null/undefined, which matches nothing, so `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined. The previous code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Google's `events.update` then gets an undefined calendarId for bookings without a stored external calendar id. The lookup should match on the destination's credential or simply take the main destination's externalId.

findings.title: deleteEvent has the same broken destination lookup
findings.body: `calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only matches when externalCalendarId is truthy, but in the fallback branch it is falsy, so the lookup always returns undefined. Deletes for bookings without an explicit external calendar id silently go to 'primary' instead of the booked calendar, leaving the event behind on the real calendar.

findings.title: Lark always uses the first destination calendar, ignoring the per-credential target
findings.body: createEvent (and createAttendees/updateEvent/deleteEvent) derive the calendar id from `event.destinationCalendar[0]` only. Since EventManager now calls createEvent once per destination (passing `destination.externalId`), every Lark credential creates its event on the first host's calendar. For collective events with multiple hosts, the second host's Lark event is created in the wrong calendar and duplicates are placed on the first host's calendar. The explicit externalId/credential is never used.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent ignores the per-host destination calendar
findings.body: createEvent always uses `event.destinationCalendar[0]` for the target calendar. With multiple destinations (collective event), EventManager invokes createEvent for each host credential, but the Office365 service ignores which credential it belongs to and writes every host's event into the first host's calendar. The PR's goal of inviting each host correctly is not met for Outlook.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents may pass undefined credential to updateEvent
findings.body: After the DB fallback, `credential` may still be undefined (the DB lookup can return null or a credential without app slug). The code then unconditionally pushes `updateEvent(credential, ...)`, which calls getCalendar(undefined) and will throw inside an un-awaited promise, or be caught as a generic error. Unlike the create path, there is no `if (credential)` guard. Also, `credential` is a shared outer variable reused across loop iterations, so a stale value from a previous reference can be used.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes events once per calendar reference
findings.body: The bookingCalendarReference loop now iterates every calendar reference. Inside, the recurring branch (`allRemainingBookings`) re-runs the whole loop over all user calendar credentials and all updatedBookings, so with N calendar references each remaining booking's event is deleted N times. Duplicate deleteEvent calls push duplicate promises into apiDeletes and can produce spurious errors. The recurring deletion should run once outside the per-reference loop.

findings.title: Dynamic-user query drops organization select and adds broad error mapping
findings.body: In the loadUsers rewrite, the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` clause was removed from the dynamic user findMany. Downstream code that relies on organization slug for dynamic group bookings will now get undefined. The new try/catch also converts every non-HttpError/non-Prisma error into a generic 500 'Unable to load users', hiding the real cause, and treats an empty dynamicUserList as a 400 that previously could have been handled differently.

findings.title: Collective co-host destination calendars dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: Team destination calendars are appended with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`. If the organizer has no destinationCalendar, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` and the push is silently skipped, so the other collective hosts' calendars are never added, which is the exact case this PR is meant to fix. The array should be initialized before pushing.

findings.title: PR ships no tests for multi-destination behavior
findings.body: The PR changes the destinationCalendar contract across ~20 files (array shape, per-credential selection, fallbacks) but adds no unit or e2e tests. The checklist explicitly says tests were not added. The collective multi-host scenario and the array-to-single fallbacks are untested, which is how the regressions above slipped through.
